- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If model consistently underpredicts true outcomes in early days of 30d horizon, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative trend over 3–5 days, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast for next 7–10 days.
